name: Sir Keir Starmer
role: Prime Minister & First Lord of the Treasury
bio: Former Director of Public Prosecutions and QC. Elected Prime Minister in July 2024, leading the first Labour government in 14 years on five core national missions.
keyStance: Economic stability, strict fiscal guardrails, Strategic Defence Review, 10-year NHS turnaround plan, resetting relations with European allies.

name: Angela Rayner
role: Deputy Prime Minister & Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government
bio: Deputy Prime Minister and prominent grassroots trade unionist, steering the government's flagship 1.5M homes target, planning deregulation on grey belt land, and the Employment Rights Bill.
keyStance: New Deal for Working People, mandatory council housing targets, ban on Section 21 no-fault evictions, devolution of powers to regional metro mayors.

name: Rachel Reeves
bio: First female Chancellor in British history. Former Bank of England economist steering fiscal policy through her 'securonomics' doctrine of supply-side investment.
keyStance: Balancing day-to-day spending with tax receipts, reformed fiscal debt rules allowing capital borrowing, 20% VAT on private school fees, increased Employer National Insurance.

name: Yvette Cooper
bio: Former Home Affairs Select Committee Chair overseeing borders, police standards, counter-terrorism, and public safety.
keyStance: Scrapped the Rwanda scheme, established the elite Border Security Command, cross-border European policing pacts to smash smuggler gangs, neighbourhood policing guarantee.

name: David Lammy
role: Secretary of State for Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Affairs
bio: Harvard Law graduate and prominent internationalist, driving Labour's 'progressive realism' foreign policy doctrine.
keyStance: Deepening UK-EU security partnership, unshakeable support for NATO and Ukrainian sovereignty, balanced Middle East diplomacy with two-state commitment.

name: John Healey
bio: Experienced defence specialist who led the shadow brief before taking office, spearheading the comprehensive Strategic Defence Review.
keyStance: Roadmap to 2.5% of GDP defence spending, landmark UK-Germany Trinity House Defence Agreement, modernised sovereign military procurement.

name: Wes Streeting
role: Secretary of State for Health and Social Care
bio: Health reformer driving 'reform alongside investment' in the NHS, shifting focus from acute hospital care to community hubs and digital triage.
keyStance: Deliver 40,000 extra appointments a week, utilise spare private hospital capacity free for NHS patients, 10-year workforce plan, phasing in smoking ban.

name: Ed Miliband
role: Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: Former Labour leader and international climate negotiator, driving the transition to 100% clean power by 2030.
keyStance: Publicly owned Great British Energy (£8.3bn capital), lift onshore wind ban, end new North Sea oil & gas licenses, Warm Homes insulation programme.

name: Shabana Mahmood
role: Lord Chancellor & Secretary of State for Justice
bio: Barrister and senior minister managing prison overcrowding crisis, court backlogs, and judicial sentencing overhauls.
keyStance: Emergency prison capacity management, independent sentencing review, rapid court processing for violent offenders.

name: Bridget Phillipson
bio: Oxford-educated minister leading national curriculum reform, early years childcare expansion, and free school breakfast clubs.
keyStance: Expand 30 hours funded childcare, fund 6,500 new expert teachers via private school fee VAT, free breakfast clubs in all primary schools.

name: Kemi Badenoch
role: Leader of the Opposition & Conservative Leader
bio: Elected Conservative Party leader in November 2024. Former Business and Trade Secretary and Equalities Minister, emphasizing institutional reform, free enterprise, and rebuilding trust.
keyStance: Roll back state intervention, defend family enterprise and farming inheritance reliefs, dismantle civil service quangos, reduce welfare dependency.

name: Mel Stride
bio: Former Treasury Select Committee Chair and Work and Pensions Secretary, leading forensic economic scrutiny of government budgets.
keyStance: Oppose employer National Insurance tax hikes, defend pensions triple lock, demand strict spending reductions across Whitehall departments.

name: Chris Philp
bio: Former Policing and Crime Minister, focusing on border security, immigration deterrence, and visible neighbourhood law enforcement.
keyStance: Demand legal caps on net migration, tough custodial sentences for knife crime, restore third-country deportation deterrence.

name: Dame Priti Patel
bio: Former Home Secretary and International Development Secretary, championing bilateral global trade and robust international deterrence.
keyStance: Strong deterrent posture against hostile authoritarian states, defend Atlantic security alliance, resist EU institutional realignment.

name: James Cartlidge
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Defence
bio: Former Defence Procurement Minister with deep insight into military supply chains and frontline equipment modernization.
keyStance: Legislate 2.5% of GDP defence spending by 2030, ring-fence Dreadnought nuclear submarine replacement, protect British Army headcount floor.

name: Robert Jenrick
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Justice
bio: Leadership runner-up and former Immigration Minister, vocal advocate for leaving the ECHR and tough justice sentencing.
keyStance: Leave the European Convention on Human Rights (ECHR) to expedite foreign criminal deportations, expand prison capacity.

name: Claire Coutinho
role: Shadow Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
bio: Former Energy Secretary, leading the Conservative critique of Great British Energy and green levies on household bills.
keyStance: Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing, Small Modular Nuclear Reactors (SMRs), oppose rapid green mandates that inflate domestic bills.

name: Nigel Farage
bio: Brexit architect, broadcaster, and Reform UK leader elected to Parliament in 2024, spearheading populist challenge to traditional parties.
keyStance: Freeze non-essential immigration, leave ECHR, raise income tax threshold to £20,000, scrap Net Zero targets, independent patient healthcare choice.

name: Richard Tice
bio: Businessman and property entrepreneur serving as Reform UK's deputy leader and economic spokesperson.
keyStance: Cut corporation tax to 15%, lift employer National Insurance thresholds, unleash UK shale and North Sea gas, abolish IR35.

name: Lee Anderson
role: Chief Whip & Spokesperson for Working Class Issues
bio: Former coal miner and former Conservative Deputy Chairman, widely followed for blunt populist commentary and working-class representation.
keyStance: Zero tolerance on illegal boat crossings, immediate detention and removal, stop taxpayer funding of hotel accommodations for migrants.

name: Rupert Lowe
bio: Former football chairman and businessman campaigning against excessive civil service bureaucracy and farm inheritance taxes.
keyStance: Slash Whitehall staffing by 50%, protect family farms from inheritance tax, scrap green subsidies inflating energy costs.

name: Sir Ed Davey
bio: Former Energy Secretary who led the Liberal Democrats to a historic 72 MPs in 2024, focusing on health, social care, and local services.
keyStance: Universal access to GP appointments within 7 days, £5bn free personal adult care package, ban water executive bonuses, rejoin EU Single Market.

name: Daisy Cooper
bio: Deputy Leader and former Health Spokesperson, leading the Lib Dem economic push on fair taxation and public service reinvestment.
keyStance: Tax big tech monopolies and bank super-profits, reverse threshold stealth taxes, support small high-street businesses.

name: Helen Morgan
role: Spokesperson for Health and Social Care
bio: Chartered accountant and by-election victor, leading the party's campaigns on rural ambulance wait times and dental deserts.
keyStance: Dedicated fund for ambulance waiting times, mental health parity in all NHS trusts, free personal social care.

name: Calum Miller
role: Spokesperson for Defence and Foreign Affairs
bio: Former senior civil servant with extensive foreign policy and defence background.
keyStance: Meet 2.5% GDP defence spending responsibly, strengthen NATO European pillar, uphold international humanitarian law.

name: Carla Denyer
bio: Renewable energy engineer elected MP for Bristol Central; prominent voice on social housing, wealth taxation, and NHS restoration.
keyStance: 1% to 2% annual wealth tax on fortunes over £10m, local rent controls, scrap Trident nuclear weapons, end NHS privatisation.

name: Adrian Ramsay
bio: Environmental strategist and co-leader elected MP for rural Waveney Valley.
keyStance: Protect British biodiversity, nationalise water and railway utilities, halt all new oil and gas exploration.

name: John Swinney
role: Party Leader & First Minister of Scotland
bio: First Minister of Scotland and veteran statesman leading the Scottish Government with focus on child poverty reduction and public services.
keyStance: Scottish self-determination, scrap the two-child benefit cap across the UK, remove Trident nuclear weapons from Scotland, rejoin EU.

name: Stephen Flynn
bio: Leading SNP parliamentarian driving parliamentary scrutiny of energy transition and Scottish budget consequentials.
keyStance: Just transition for North Sea energy workers without cliff-edges, demand full devolution of employment and migration powers.

name: Rhun ap Iorwerth
role: Party Leader & Member of the Senedd
bio: Former BBC journalist and Plaid Cymru leader, uniting the party around fair funding formulas, Welsh NHS renewal, and independence.
keyStance: Replace Barnett formula with needs-based funding (+£1.2bn/yr), reclaim £4bn HS2 rail consequentials, devolve Crown Estate to Wales.

name: Liz Saville Roberts
bio: Privy Councillor and Westminster leader campaigning for judicial devolution and equal treatment of Wales.
keyStance: Devolution of policing and criminal justice to Wales, renewable wealth retention for Welsh communities.

name: Movement Council Spokesperson
bio: Civic assembly representing traditionalist British restoration, civil liberties, and free-market constitutionalism.
keyStance: Abolish Net Zero statutes, repeal legislation eroding free speech, constitutional referendums, national industrial revival.
